static_findings.snippet: **CRITICAL**: Do NOT use example imports like `THREE.OrbitControls` - they won't work on the CDN.
**IMPORTANT**: Do NOT use `CapsuleGeometry` (introduced in r142, not available in r128)
**Skip lighting** if using `MeshBasicMaterial` - it's unlit by design.
Since `THREE.OrbitControls` isn't available on CDN, implement custom controls:
- Always set `antialias: true` on renderer for smooth edges
- ❌ Forgetting to add objects to scene with `scene.add()`
- ❌ Forgetting to call `renderer.render()` in animation loop
- Position lights thoughtfully - avoid overlapping multiple bright lights

content.value_statement: Building browser 3D scenes is error-prone because setup, lighting, controls, and performance must work together. This skill provides practical Three.js patterns for reliable scenes, animations, and interactions.
actual_capabilities: Guides setup for Three.js r128 with scene, camera, renderer, and animation loop.
Explains geometry, material, lighting, and resize patterns for browser scenes.
Shows mouse interaction, custom camera control, raycasting, and hover selection patterns.
Provides particle, texture, shadow, environment map, fog, and grouping examples.
Compares CDN prototypes with production build tool workflows and common libraries.
limitations: It is a Markdown guidance skill and does not include executable source files.
Examples focus on Three.js r128 CDN compatibility, not every current Three.js feature.
Generated scenes still need browser testing for layout, performance, and rendering errors.
It does not provide bundled 3D models, textures, or asset licensing guidance.

use_cases.title: Prototype Interactive 3D UI
use_cases.description: Create quick browser scenes with animation, lighting, resize handling, and mouse interaction.

use_cases.title: Explain 3D Rendering Concepts
use_cases.description: Teach Three.js foundations through clear examples for geometry, materials, cameras, and lights.

use_cases.title: Plan Production WebGL Work
use_cases.description: Move from simple CDN demos toward build tools, loaders, animation libraries, and performance patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Rotating Object
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Three.js skill to create a responsive browser scene with a rotating object, camera, renderer, lighting, and animation loop.

prompt_templates.title: Interactive 3D Scene
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Three.js skill to design an interactive 3D scene where users can move the camera, hover objects, and select items.

prompt_templates.title: Polished Visual Demo
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Three.js skill to build a polished visual demo with shadows, environment lighting, particles, responsive resizing, and smooth animation.

prompt_templates.title: Production Architecture Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Three.js skill to plan a production Three.js implementation with build tools, loaders, animation libraries, and performance safeguards.

output_examples.input: Create a responsive rotating planet scene with stars and mouse movement.
output_examples.output: A browser-ready Three.js scene plan with camera placement, sphere geometry, star particles, lighting, resize behavior, and animation steps.

output_examples.input: Make a clickable 3D product selector for three objects.
output_examples.output: An interaction design that uses raycasting, hover scaling, selected object styling, camera controls, and a continuous render loop.

output_examples.input: Improve a Three.js demo for portfolio presentation.
output_examples.output: A refinement checklist covering antialiasing, shadows, tone mapping, environment maps, asset loading, and performance limits.

best_practices: Start with scene, camera, renderer, resize handling, and a working render loop before adding complexity.
Choose materials and lights together so objects remain visible and visually consistent.
Limit geometry detail and particle counts until performance is tested on target devices.
anti_patterns: Do not use Three.js features that are unavailable in the targeted runtime version.
Do not add lit materials without matching lights, because scenes may render black.
Do not skip browser testing, because WebGL errors often appear only at runtime.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps create browser-based Three.js scenes, animations, visual effects, particles, and interactive 3D elements.

faq.question: Does the skill include executable code files?
faq.answer: No. It is a Markdown instruction skill that guides an AI agent when writing Three.js code.

faq.question: Which Three.js version does it emphasize?
faq.answer: It emphasizes Three.js r128 for CDN-compatible demos and explains when production projects should use newer build workflows.

faq.question: Can it help with user interaction?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers mouse movement, custom camera controls, raycasting, click handling, and hover feedback.

faq.question: Can it support production projects?
faq.answer: It provides planning guidance for production stacks, but final projects still need testing, asset management, and performance review.

faq.question: Is network access required by the skill itself?
faq.answer: The skill file does not perform network requests. Its examples may reference a public Three.js CDN for generated browser demos.
